title: Numbers, Quantities & SI Units
pedagogicalStatus: Unreviewed author draft; formative practice only

sources.title: A Virtual Measurement Table
paragraphs: These are example values for language practice, not measurements from a real laboratory.
Sample A: length — 0.35 m (meter). Sample B: mass — 0.80 kg (kilogram).
Sample C: time interval — 12.5 s (second). Sample D: electric current — 0.20 A (ampere).
Sample E: temperature — 295 K (kelvin). Sample F: voltage — 4.5 V (volt).
Sample G: force — 3.0 N (newton). Sample H: energy — 6.0 J (joule).
A quantity is what we measure; a unit states how its value is expressed. Write a space before an SI unit symbol. Symbols do not have a plural -s.

sources.title: Nora's Measurement Desk
paragraphs: Nora has a ruler, a digital scale, and a timer. She records the length of a small block as 0.24 m, its mass as 0.60 kg, and a time interval as 8.5 s.
Nora says: 'There is some equipment on the desk.' She can also say: 'There are three instruments on the desk.'
Her classmate asks, 'How many measurements did you record?' She answers, 'Three.' He asks, 'How much time did you measure?' She replies, 'Eight point five seconds.'

sources.title: Workshop Notice
paragraphs: The room temperature display reads 22 °C. A small mass has a value of 0.25 kg. The timer is set to 30 s.
A demonstration uses 3 V. A straight line is approximately 2 m long.
V is the symbol for the volt, a unit used to express voltage. The symbol °C refers to degree Celsius, not to coulomb.

sources.title: A Class Discussion of Numbers
paragraphs: The instructor asks, 'Are thirteen and thirty the same?' Kai says, 'No: thirteen is 13, but thirty is 30.'
'And read 1/2.' Kai says, 'One-half or a half.'
'Which is larger: 0.6 or 0.06?' Kai answers, 'Zero point six is larger.'

items.prompt: A ruler is introduced for the first time. I need ___ ruler.
items.feedback: Ruler begins with a consonant sound; use a.

items.prompt: An ammeter is introduced for the first time. She has ___ ammeter.
items.feedback: Ammeter begins with a vowel sound; use an.

items.prompt: Choose the article for a newly introduced instrument: There is ___ instrument.
items.feedback: Instrument begins with a vowel sound.

items.prompt: Complete: Nora has a ruler. ___ ruler is on the desk.
items.feedback: Use the for a specific ruler already mentioned.

items.prompt: Complete: We need ___ voltmeter for the example.
items.feedback: The word voltmeter begins with a consonant sound.

items.prompt: Complete: I see a display. ___ display shows 22 °C.
items.feedback: Use the to refer back to the introduced display.

items.prompt: Choose the natural English phrase.
items.feedback: Equipment is ordinarily uncountable in this meaning.

items.prompt: Choose the natural English phrase.
items.feedback: Measurement is countable; the plural is measurements.

items.prompt: Which noun is generally uncountable in this meaning?
items.feedback: Information is an uncountable noun in ordinary academic English.

items.prompt: Complete: There are two ___ on the desk.
items.feedback: Use the plural form instruments after two.

items.prompt: Complete: ___ time do we have?
items.feedback: Use how much with uncountable time.

items.prompt: Complete: ___ measurements are in the table?
items.feedback: Use how many with countable plural measurements.

items.prompt: Complete: We have ___ equipment in the cabinet.
items.feedback: Use some with the uncountable noun equipment.

items.prompt: Complete: Two ___ are on the table. (timer)
items.feedback: Add -s to make the plural timers.

items.prompt: Which is the correct SI unit symbol for two meters?
items.feedback: SI unit symbols do not take plural endings.

items.prompt: How do we read the number 0.05?
items.feedback: Read each digit after the decimal point.

items.prompt: Which numeral represents thirteen?
items.feedback: Thirteen is 13; thirty is 30.

items.prompt: Choose a natural way to read 1/2.
items.feedback: The fraction 1/2 can be read one-half or a half.

items.prompt: Which value is larger?
items.feedback: Six tenths is larger than six hundredths.

items.prompt: What does approximately mean?
items.feedback: Approximately signals a close estimate, not necessarily an exact value.

items.prompt: Which quantity is expressed in kilograms?
items.feedback: The kilogram (kg) is the SI base unit of mass.

items.prompt: Which quantity is expressed in seconds?
items.feedback: The second (s) is the SI base unit of time.

items.prompt: What is the unit symbol for the volt?
items.feedback: The symbol V stands for volt.

items.prompt: What is the symbol for the kelvin?
items.feedback: The kelvin has symbol K, without a degree sign.

items.prompt: Choose the correctly spaced SI value.
items.feedback: Write a space between a numerical value and its unit symbol.

items.prompt: What length appears for sample A?
items.feedback: The table lists sample A's length as 0.35 m.

items.prompt: What unit is used for sample D's electric current?
items.feedback: The unit for current in the table is ampere.

items.prompt: What temperature is listed for sample E?
items.feedback: Sample E records a temperature of 295 K.

items.prompt: How many measurements does Nora write?
items.feedback: Nora records length, mass and a time interval.

items.prompt: What time interval does Nora record?
items.feedback: The time interval in Nora's record is 8.5 s.

items.prompt: What does the room-temperature display show?
items.feedback: The workshop notice displays 22 °C.

items.prompt: What voltage does the demonstration use?
items.feedback: The notice states a demonstration voltage of 3 V.

items.prompt: Which is larger according to the discussion?
items.feedback: Kai says that 0.6 is larger than 0.06.

items.prompt: What number is described as thirty?
items.feedback: Thirty represents the number 30.
